situation: In March, the Benue at Garoua is shallow and the sandbanks are visible. In September, after months of rain, the river is wide and full.
Mohamadou wonders where the water of the Benue comes from and where it goes, since the river never stops flowing.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Mohamadou does not understand where the water of the Benue comes from and where it goes.
How does the Benue change between March and September?
In March, it is shallow with sandbanks. In September, it is wide and full.
How can the people of Garoua help to keep water in the Benue?
They can plant trees along the banks, avoid polluting the river and use water carefully.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the continuous movement of water between the sea, the air and the land.

qa.q: Water moves from the sea to the air, to the land and back to the sea, again and again. What is this called?
qa.a: It is called the hydrological cycle, or water cycle. It is powered by the energy of the sun.

qa.q: Name the processes by which water goes up into the air.
qa.a: Water goes up by evaporation from seas, lakes and rivers, and by transpiration from the leaves of plants.

qa.q: After rain falls on the land, what are the two ways in which it returns to rivers?
qa.a: It flows over the ground as surface runoff, or it soaks into the ground (infiltration) and flows slowly as groundwater.

sum.title: I. Meaning and Components
defs: The hydrological cycle is the continuous movement of water between the oceans, the atmosphere and the land, powered by the sun.
items: Evaporation is the change of liquid water into water vapour. Transpiration is the loss of water vapour by plants through their leaves.
Condensation turns water vapour into droplets that form clouds. Precipitation brings the water back to the Earth as rain, hail or snow.
Infiltration is the soaking of water into the ground. Surface runoff is the flow of water over the ground into rivers and the sea.

qa.title: Question 1
qa.q: In the drainage basin of the Benue, water enters as rain and leaves by evaporation and river flow. Why is it called an open system?
qa.a: It is an open system because water enters it (input) and leaves it (output). Between them, water is stored and transferred.

qa.q: Is the global water cycle open or closed? Explain.
qa.a: The global cycle is a closed system for water: the total amount of water on Earth stays the same. Only energy from the sun enters and leaves.

sum.title: II. The Hydrological Cycle as an Open System
sum.intro: At the scale of a drainage basin, the hydrological cycle is an open system, with inputs, stores, transfers and outputs:
items: Water is stored on leaves (interception), on the surface, in the soil and as groundwater. It is transferred by infiltration, runoff and throughflow.
Water leaves by evaporation, transpiration and river flow to the sea.
At the scale of the whole Earth, the water cycle is a closed system: the total amount of water does not change.

sum.title: III. Diagram of the Hydrological Cycle
items: Copy the diagram with its labels: evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, surface runoff, infiltration and groundwater flow.

evaluation: What is the difference between evaporation and transpiration?
Evaporation is water vapour coming from water surfaces, while transpiration is water vapour released by plants.
Why is the drainage basin an open system?
It is an open system because water enters it as precipitation and leaves it by evaporation and river flow.
How does cutting trees affect the water cycle?
It reduces transpiration and infiltration, and increases surface runoff, floods and soil erosion.
remediation: The continuous movement of water is the ______ cycle.
Water vapour lost by plants is ______.
Water soaking into the ground is ______.
Water flowing over the ground is surface ______.
The input of a drainage basin is ______.
At the global scale, the water cycle is a ______ system.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. hydrological 2. transpiration 3. infiltration 4. runoff 5. precipitation 6. closed
end.homework: Ask your grandparents or an elder whether the dry season is hotter or longer today than when they were young. Write down what they say.
teacherNote: Correction of the source notes: the global water cycle is a closed system for water (only energy enters and leaves). The syllabus "open system" refers to the drainage basin, where water enters and leaves.
Part III is mainly for copying the labelled diagram.
